title: Billboard Acquires ‘Cosmic Symphony,’ Laura Karpman Documentary On Iconic Instruments Lost In LA Wildfires: “A Requiem And A Celebration”
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew ‘I’m Doing My Job’ Trailer: Six Women ER Docs Combat Covid, Raise Kids In Aneri Shah’s Directorial Debut Brilliance Of The Who’s Leader Shines In ‘Pete Townshend: Behind Blue Eyes,’ Screening At Hamptons & Mill Valley ‘Speak.’ Is Spoken For: Documentary+ To Stream Film About High School Oratory Competitors View All October 5, 2026 10:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The remains of Starr Parodi's piano, an instrument used in the score for 'The Wizard of Oz,' are recovered from the ashes of the LA wildfires. Billboard EXCLUSIVE: Billboard has acquired Cosmic Symphony , the directorial debut of Oscar-nominated composer Laura Karpman that explores irreplaceable musical instruments lost in the Los Angeles wildfires, and the artists who owned them. EGOT winner John Legend, two-time Academy Award winner Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy, and actress, singer and songwriter Rita Wilson are among the executive producers of the short documentary. Billboard plans to launch the film on its digital channels and Billboard TV (available on Amazon Fire and Samsung TV+) on Tuesday, October 27. The night before – Monday, October 26 – the film’s Los Angeles premiere will take place at the Wallis Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts in Beverly Hills. Related Stories News Laura Karpman Hid An Alan Silvestri Homage In Music For 'Captain America: Brave New World' - Sound & Screen Film News Deadline's Sound & Screen: Film Sets Lineup For 2025 Edition, From 'Kpop Demon Hunters' To Kesha, Oscar Winners Ludwig Göransson, Alexandre Desplat, Michael Giacchino & More Each of the four musicians featured in the documentary – bassist and composer John Clayton, pianist and educator Susie Chung, pianist and composer Starr Parodi, and composer, guitarist and pianist Diane Warren – suffered terrible losses in the January 2025 wildfires, including beloved instruments. One of Clayton’s basses destroyed when fire consumed his home in Altadena was almost 200 years old and had been owned formerly by bassist Ray Brown. Watch on Deadline John Clayton on bass in ‘Cosmic Symphony’ (an animation overlays the instrument). Courtesy of Billboard “ Cosmic Symphony explores a truth that every musician knows – that musical instruments have souls,” notes a release. “Four iconic instruments, including The Wizard of Oz and A Star is Born pianos, all lost in the 2025 Los Angeles Fires, are celebrated by John Clayton, Susie Chung, Starr Parodi and Diane Warren, culminating in an animated send-off towards an imagined future, a Cosmic Symphony.” Karpman directed the film and composed the original score. In a statement, she said, “When a musician loses an instrument, they lose a part of themselves – their partner, their voice. In the aftermath of the Los Angeles Fires, I felt a strong sense of urgency; my friends, musicians across Los Angeles, were experiencing profound loss, and their experiences needed to be captured. I envisioned this film, my first as a director, simultaneously as a requiem and a celebration. Somewhere in the heavens, these beloved instruments have formed a glorious orchestra—a cosmic symphony where every lost voice is restored. “ Cosmic Symphony memorializes the instruments, honors their journeys, and affirms the resilience of the human spirit. Each instrument lost represents a story interrupted, a melody waiting to be continued. Music, after all, is the language of survival—the force that keeps us connected even in the face of devastation.” The film is produced by Laura Karpman and Lorenza Muñoz. Along with Legend, Obaid-Chinoy, and Wilson, executive producers include Mike Jackson, Legend’s partner at Get Lifted Film Co, Christina Kounelias, and Peter Rotter. Amy Andersson is a co-producer. Diane Warren at the piano, with H.E.R. on guitar in ‘Cosmic Symphony.’ Courtesy of Billboard “Artists are the beating heart of Los Angeles, the creative capitol of the world,” Legend commented. “As artists, we know that instruments are core to the music we make. Cosmic Symphony is a thank you to all of the musical instruments that help us sing our song. As we look back on the immense tragedy of the fires of 2025, I’m inspired by the stories of loss and resilience that are portrayed in this film. I am so happy to join my friend Laura Karpman in celebrating the music of our city.” Jackson added, “ Cosmic Symphony is a beautiful reminder of how deeply music is tied to memory, identity and community. Laura has created something that honors what was lost while also celebrating the artists and stories that endure. We’re proud to be part of a film that captures the resilience of Los Angeles and the extraordinary role music plays in bringing people together.” Wilson’s work in music includes the albums AM/FM , Rita Wilson , Bigger Picture , and Halfway to Home . “Laura Karpman’s short documentary film, Cosmic Symphony , illuminates for us how instruments are not inanimate objects that have no life,” Wilson observed. “They are our friends, our confidants, our family. And just like those friends and family, they have lives that preceded, sometimes even our own lives. They bring their history to each musician who plays them, and to each of us who listens. It’s been an honor being a part of this film. I doubt I will ever be able to look at an instrument in the same way again without the distinct feeling that each instrument has had a life of its own.” The Los Angeles premiere on October 26 at the Annenberg will be followed by a concert performance featuring the musicians in the film and more. All ticket proceeds will go towards MusiCares, the nonprofit that provides health, financial, and emergency relief services to professional musicians. Composer Laura Karpman seen onstage at Deadline’s 2025 Sound & Screen Film held at UCLA’s Royce Hall on November 5, 2025 in Los Angeles. JC Olivera/Deadline via Getty Images Karpman’s composing credits include 2023’s American Fiction , for which she earned an Academy Award nomination; East of Eden (2026); Give Me the Ball! (2026); The Marvels (2023), and Lovecraft Country (2020). She directed Cosmic Symphony and produced the film alongside Lorenza Muñoz. Michael Wohl and Kate Amend edited Cosmic Symphony . Cinematography is by Christina Dunlap; Temple Hale serves as animation director. Sound is by Paul Hollman. The partnership is The Black List’s first with an independent publisher. Spiegel & Grau are best known for award-winning books such as Just Mercy by Bryan Stevenson and Piper Kerman’s Orange is the New Black and recent bestsellers Beartooth by Callan Wink, The Fire Agent by David Baerwald and Margaret Renkl’s The Comfort of Crows. Spiegel & Grau books can be found via searching by title, author, genre and other associated book information available on blcklst.com . Metadata provided by Spiegel & Grau includes additional information such as a published book’s imprint, book cover art, book description, and more. This initiative also makes it easier for Spiegel & Grau authors to list their published books in their Black List profile quickly and efficiently, according to S&G. Liza Wachter, Spiegel & Grau President and Director of Film and Television, said, “This partnership opens our catalog to the film and television industry in a new way. We’re proud to be the first independent publisher to partner with The Black List.” “As a reader, I’ve been a fan of Spiegel & Grau for most of my adult life; it is a dream to be partnering with them on this initiative, The Black List’s second with a trade publisher, our first with an indie publisher.
